subject.title: fix: stop doctor misreporting trusted-proxy gateways as unauthenticated

question: Should a non-loopback Gateway with fully runtime-valid trusted-proxy authentication be reported by Doctor as warning-level network exposure rather than as an unauthenticated critical?
rationale: This is a deliberate security-diagnostic severity policy, not a mechanical correctness question; the code can mirror runtime contracts while maintainers still decide the operator-facing posture.

options.title: Accept the guarded warning policy
options.body: Approve the trusted-proxy warning path after current-head proof shows valid configurations downgrade while invalid and skipped exec-secret configurations remain critical.

options.title: Retain the unauthenticated critical
options.body: Keep the existing conservative diagnostic for every non-loopback trusted-proxy deployment until a different product security policy is defined.

recommendation.title: Accept the guarded warning policy
recommendation.body: Approve the trusted-proxy warning path after current-head proof shows valid configurations downgrade while invalid and skipped exec-secret configurations remain critical.

likelyOwner.reason: A current Gateway/Doctor area owner should decide the operator-facing security severity because the available evidence cannot safely assign an individual.
